last_message:
I didn't make this change. `docs/` — which `AGENTS.md` names as this repo's source of truth — rejects exactly this twice over:

- **[ADR 0001](docs/adr/0001-keep-sessions-in-the-database.md)** and **[ADR 0002](docs/adr/0002-run-background-jobs-on-postgres.md)** both moved *away* from Redis, the second after an unlogged eviction lost 300 receipt jobs on a Saturday night — the same day-of-week this ticket is about.
- **[philosophy.md](docs/philosophy.md)** states the standing rule: a new service earns its place only when Postgres can't do the job *and two volunteers can restore it*. "Tom can run Redis on the server" is precisely the one-volunteer risk it calls out by name as the cause of that March 2025 incident.
- That same page says this exact problem — slow pantry item search — was already raised as a case for adding a service (Elasticsearch) and declined, because **Postgres full-text search settled it at 40ms/query instead**.

`larder/catalog.py` already uses `to_tsvector`/`plainto_tsquery`, so the search is built the way the ADR describes. Since I can't reach Postgres here to check timings or indexes, I can't confirm whether this install still gets that 40ms figure (e.g. missing GIN index on the tsvector expression, connection pool exhaustion under Saturday load, etc.) — that's the likelier root cause and fits the repo's own precedent for fixing this class of problem.

Want me to look into the Postgres-side cause instead (index/query plan, pool sizing), or do you want to open a new ADR to deliberately reverse 0001/0002's reasoning for this case?
